summary: The current proposal explicitly addresses the earlier Smart Add binding-retention, SSE, ownership-disclosure, dependent-action and AI lifecycle gaps. Its immutable-command, ACK/feed, snapshot/live-queue, generation, worker-fence and restore safeguards are specified as future requirements, not tested implementation. One consequential contradiction remains: the generic legacy replay mapping rejects a colliding consent revoke that the accepted privacy contract requires to succeed. Owner approvals, empirical sizing and implementation acceptance remain separate disclosed gates; this review supplies none of them.

findings.description: Preserve the accepted consent-revocation collision exception before routing Navigator through the generic legacy receipt boundary. A supported client may grant cloud consent using key K and then revoke using the same K. The accepted endpoint deliberately returns 204, revokes all grants, preserves the original grant receipt, and records a separate deterministic revoke receipt. Sync v1 instead mandates one legacy receipt per (owner, key), forbids an operation-specific replay namespace, and rejects changed content before execution. Applied to PR-28, that rule returns an idempotency conflict without revoking consent, leaving subsequent cloud requests authorized after a revocation that must succeed. The current proposal simultaneously promises legacy response/error and owner-wide revoke compatibility, so the implementation contract is contradictory.
evidence: specs/026-rust-core-sync/contracts/sync-v1.md:57 requires one durable command receipt for the legacy (owner_id, idempotency_key) identity and prohibits changing the replay namespace when the operation changes; :60 rejects the same command ID with changed content and executes nothing.

specs/026-rust-core-sync/tasks.md:87 (T028 / PR-28) explicitly routes Navigator consent-grant and owner-wide-revoke through this shared command boundary. contracts/command-catalog.md:35 promises the current owner-wide revoke semantics; spec.md FR-014/019/024 require legacy compatibility and current consent.

specs/020-weekly-review/contracts/http.md:696-708 explicitly distinguishes grant conflicts from revocation: a key another command already stored must still revoke, preserve that record, and store a separate replayable revoke result.

backend/app/modules/tasks/navigator.py:890-930 implements the exception by checking the collision receipt before revoking and storing the result under _revoke_collision_key when the original key is occupied.

backend/tests/test_review_navigator.py:1271-1306 contains existing tests for grant(K1) then revoke(K1) succeeding and a later replay of that colliding revoke not cancelling a newer grant. These tests were inspected, not executed.
findings.recommendation: Document a narrow legacy Navigator revoke mapping that preserves its accepted collision identity before generic mismatch rejection, while publishing the revoke and its receipt/feed atomically through the same boundary. Preserve the original grant receipt and deterministic revoke replay so a late revoke retry cannot cancel a subsequent regrant; do not weaken ordinary command-ID mismatch rejection. Reuse the two existing collision tests through the migrated adapter and reflect the exception in the catalog/data-model mapping.
